hints: Look carefully at where X is pointing. It is the thick middle wall layer around the small central lumen, not the very thin inner lining or the outer coat.
Remember what an artery wall must do: stretch and recoil with high pressure, squeeze to control flow, and resist bursting. Which three tissues give those three jobs?
walkthrough:
**Identify Layer X**

Look at the diagram. You see a small central lumen with a very thick wall around it. That is classic artery structure.

Layer X is the thick middle layer, called the tunica media.

**Recall What The Tunica Media Does**

Arteries carry blood at very high pressure straight from the heart. So this layer must be strong, stretchy and able to contract.

That means it needs three tissues working together: smooth muscle to contract and narrow the lumen, elastic fibres to stretch and recoil, and collagen to give tensile strength and prevent bursting.

**Choose The Complete Answer**

Because all three tissues are present in the tunica media of an artery, the only complete list is elastic fibres, collagen and smooth muscle.

options.A: This is incomplete because it leaves out elastic fibres, which are essential in arteries for stretching and recoiling with each pulse of high pressure blood.
options.B: This is incomplete because it leaves out smooth muscle, which is abundant in the tunica media for vasoconstriction and control of blood flow.
options.C: This is incomplete because it leaves out collagen, which provides tensile strength to stop the artery wall tearing under high pressure.
options.D: This is correct because the tunica media (layer X) of an artery contains smooth muscle, elastic fibres and collagen together.
